title: Infinitesimal lifting of algebraically trivial rigidified line modules
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $A\to S$ be a proper smooth commutative group algebraic space of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space] with geometric fibres abelian varieties, meaning smooth proper geometrically connected group schemes. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; smoothness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Let $T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of affine $S$-schemes defined by a quasi-coherent ideal $I$ with $I^2=0$. A line module on $A_{T_0}$ is a module on its small etale site locally isomorphic to its structure module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $(M_0,r_0)$ be such a line module, rigidified along the identity section, whose restriction to every geometric fibre is algebraically equivalent to the trivial module. Here algebraic equivalence is generated by pairs of fibres of a line-module family over a connected smooth parameter variety. There is an etale covering $\{U_i\to T\}$ and line modules $M_i$ on $A_{U_i}$, rigidified along the identity and algebraically trivial on every geometric fibre, with rigidification-preserving isomorphisms $M_i|_{A_{U_i\times_TT_0}}\simeq M_0|_{A_{U_i\times_TT_0}}$. No uniqueness of lifts is asserted. This lifting assertion also holds after replacing $S$ by any locally Noetherian base change.

proof.text: Put $B=A_T$, $B_0=A_{T_0}$, $f:B\to T$, and $f_0:B_0\to T_0$. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], these base changes are smooth and flat. On affine etale charts, tensoring $0\to I\to\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal O_{T_0}\to0$ with the flat structure algebra identifies the ideal of $B_0\hookrightarrow B$ with $J=\mathcal O_{B_0}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}I$. It is square-zero. The same calculation on $C=B\times_TB$ gives ideal $K=\mathcal O_{C_0}\otimes I$ for $C_0=B_0\times_{T_0}B_0$.

source.place: Tag 04TA, lemma-smooth-flat; affine flat tensor calculation

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-space-picard-obstruction-natural] to obtain $o=\delta_B[M_0]\in H^2(B_0,J)$. The coefficient module $I$ on $T_0$ is well defined because $I^2=0$. By [lem-sfb-algebraically-trivial-line-multiplicativity], addition on $B_0$ satisfies $m_0^*M_0\simeq p_{1,0}^*M_0\otimes p_{2,0}^*M_0$. Naturality for the three maps $C\to B$ and additivity of $\delta_C$ give
$$m_0^*o=\delta_C[m_0^*M_0]=\delta_C[p_{1,0}^*M_0]+\delta_C[p_{2,0}^*M_0]=p_{1,0}^*o+p_{2,0}^*o.$$
All coefficient maps here are the maps to $K$ of Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0DNM, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening, exact sequence and proof via a -> 1+a; pullback naturality is the naturality of that units exact sequence and its connecting map.

proof.text: Since $T_0$ is affine, use [lem-sfb-abelian-h2-reduced-coproduct-injective] with base parameter $T_0$ and $N=\Gamma(T_0,I)$. It applies to this arbitrary module, even when $T_0$ is not Noetherian. The equation of Step 2 is $D(o)=0$, so $o=0$. Exactness in [lem-sfb-space-picard-obstruction-natural] supplies a line module $L$ on $B$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:L|_{B_0}\simeq M_0$.

source.place: Chapter 6, coherent cohomology and the group-law obstruction calculation used for Proposition 6.7 (WANTED). This is an agent-stated cohomological prerequisite, not a quotation of an unread proposition. Field Hopf-algebra construction: Milne AV I, before Lemma 12.2, printed p.55 (there for etale rather than coherent cohomology).

proof.text: Let $P=e_T^*L$ and set $M=L\otimes f^*P^{-1}$, rigidified by evaluation $P\otimes P^{-1}\simeq\mathcal O_T$. Put $u=r_0\circ e_{T_0}^*\alpha:P|_{T_0}\simeq\mathcal O_{T_0}$. The restriction isomorphism $M|_{B_0}\simeq M_0$ is $\alpha\otimes f_0^*((u^{-1})^\vee)$, followed by the tensor-unit map. At the identity this sends $p\otimes\lambda$ to $u(p)\lambda(u^{-1}(1))=\lambda(p)$ under $r_0$; hence it preserves rigidifications.

source.place: I section 8, identity normalization; explicit relative tensor evaluation written by Q140

proof.text: Every geometric point of $T$ factors uniquely through $T_0$, since a field kills the square-zero ideal $I$. Its fibre of $M$ is therefore isomorphic to the corresponding fibre of $M_0$, and is algebraically trivial. Take the etale covering consisting of $\operatorname{id}_T$ and this $M$. For any locally Noetherian base change $S'\to S$, properness and finite presentation persist by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and smoothness by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The geometric fibres are fibres of the original group after an algebraically closed field extension, hence satisfy the same hypothesis. The same argument applies to every affine $S'$-parameter and its square-zero ideal. No uniqueness assertion is used.
